   130	What are the benefits of using a bedside crib?
   131	Safe sleep charity The Lullaby Trust, advises that the safest place for your
   132	baby to sleep is on their own sleep surface, in the same room as you, for
   133	at least the first 6 months. Bedside cribs allow you to have your baby
   134	sleeping right next to you at night, but in the safety of their own crib. This
   135	means you can still be close to your baby without bed-sharing, which
   136	carries a risk of suffocation and overheating.
   137	Bedside cribs enable you to lean over and easily pick up your baby when
   138	feeding at night. This is especially useful if you’ve had a difficult birth or a
   139	c-section and find getting out of bed painful. You can also easily comfort
   140	your baby if they are fussing and have a good view of them while they are
   141	sleeping.
   142	How to do the baby mattress firmness test
   143	Press your hand on the centre and the sides of the mattress •
   144	A firm mattress shouldn’t mould to the shape of your hand and
   145	you’ll feel resistance – it will obviously move beneath the
   146	pressure but your hand shouldn’t sink in
   147	•
   148	When you remove your hand, the mattress should snap back
   149	and regain its shape
   150	•
   151	From a practical perspective, bedside cribs are smaller and more compact
   152	than most cots, which means they take up less space in your bedroom
   153	than a full-sized cot or cotbed.
   154	Do I need a bedside crib for my baby?
   155	You don’t have to buy a bedside crib. It's completely safe to put a baby in a
   156	regular cot from birth. But they’re a great option if you want your baby as
   157	close to you as possible at night, and for saving space. The downside is
   158	that most of these cribs only last up to 6 months and you’ll then need to
   159	move your baby into a full-sized cot or cotbed. A moses basket is a more
   160	economical option, but these can last even less time, and do not have the
   161	added features of a bedside crib such as a drop-down side, tilt, or multiple
   162	heights.
   163	How much does a bedside crib cost?
   164	It is possible to buy budget bedside cribs for under £100 but the majority
   165	we have reviewed are between £150-£300. Certain features, such as a
   166	rocking function or one-handed drop down side, tend to push the price up
   167	slightly.
